# Architecture & Direction

This document is a working reference for deciding whether a new feature fits
where this project is going. It is not a spec, and it is not fixed — update it
as reality changes. Treat "we decided against X" entries as revisitable, not
permanent, once the stated trigger condition is actually met.

**Provenance note:** an earlier version of this document was generated by
ChatGPT from the project's original one-line goal ("install VICIdial on Rocky
10"), without seeing this codebase. It proposed a full enterprise framework —
plugin ecosystem, five-tier install profiles, a dependency-graph engine, a
benchmarking subsystem — treating all of it as greenfield work. Several of
those ideas were already solved, just not in the form it imagined; others
would mean rewriting ~3,800 lines of tested, production-proven logic for
architectural elegance nobody's paying for yet. This version keeps what was
genuinely good in that document and grounds the rest in what's actually true
about this repo, as of 2026-07-20.

---

## Philosophy

This project answers a different question than most installers:

> Not "how do I install ViciDial?" but "how do I deploy a ViciDial platform I
> can trust, maintain, upgrade, and recover?"

That standard — reliability, security, maintainability, recoverability,
transparency — is what a feature should be judged against, not "does this
make the project more sophisticated."

---

## What's already built (don't re-propose these as new work)

- **Progress tracking with resume** — Parts 1 and 2 track completed steps in
  `/root/.vicidial_part1_progress` / `/root/.vicidial_part2_progress`, and
  prompt skip/re-run/quit per step on re-run.
- **Idempotency via state-checking** — Parts 3 and 4 achieve safe re-runs by
  checking real on-disk/system state before each step (e.g. "is this file
  already deployed?") rather than a separate progress file. This is a
  deliberate, different-but-valid pattern from Parts 1/2, not a gap — it
  can't drift from reality the way a progress file can.
- **Structured logging** — every script logs to `/var/log/vicidial_*` with
  colored INFO/WARNING/ERROR/SUCCESS output via `tee`.
- **Error trapping** — `set -euo pipefail` + `trap ERR` in every script, with
  line number and failing command reported.
- **Health/verification engine** — `vicidial_rocky10_audit.sh` already checks
  screen sessions, DB schema, the keepalive timer, crontab health, Perl
  modules, core services, and WebRTC/PJSIP config. As of today it also runs
  automatically at the end of Part 4 (`--skip-audit` to opt out).
- **Version configuration** — `configs/versions.conf` holds the versions that
  are actually pinnable in code today (PHP via Remi module stream, Asterisk
  vici/plain tarball versions). Not everything is pinnable this way — MariaDB
  comes from Rocky 10's native default module stream and isn't selected by
  these scripts; the file says so rather than implying false configurability.
- **Extensive real-world hardening** — four postinstall fix guides document
  Rocky-10-specific bugs already found and fixed in production (Switch.pm,
  `ps` truncation, `Asterisk::AGI.pm` empty-digits bug, chan_sip/pjsip
  websocket conflict, dual-Asterisk-instance risk, and more). This is the
  project's actual moat — a from-scratch rewrite risks losing it.

## Near-term priorities (in progress as of 2026-07-20)

1. ~~Document Part 4 in README~~ — done.
2. ~~Extract hardcoded version strings into `configs/versions.conf`~~ — done
   for PHP and Asterisk (vici + plain fallback). MariaDB pinning deferred —
   see below.
3. ~~Wire `vicidial_rocky10_audit.sh` into the install flow~~ — done, runs
   automatically at the end of Part 4, with an explicit note that FAILs for
   services outside a given node's role (e.g. `mariadb` on an Asterisk-only
   box, in a multi-server cluster) are expected, not bugs.
4. Repo-privacy / customer-data hygiene — keep production cluster specifics
   (real IPs, non-default SSH ports, carrier whitelists, client-specific IVR
   details) out of any file that ships with a distributed/sold copy of this
   repo. Split into a generic version + a local, gitignored file with real
   details, the same way credentials are already gitignored today.

## Deferred — revisit only when the trigger condition is actually met

- **Plugin architecture / SDK** — revisit once there are 3+ customers whose
  needs actually diverge (not "might diverge"). Until then, one-off
  customizations (e.g. Empire IVR) should stay as clearly-separated optional
  steps, not a formal plugin system nobody else is using yet.
- **Installation profiles (Minimal/Standard/Production/Enterprise)** —
  revisit if/when customers actually ask for different topologies. Today's
  real-world case is a two-node cluster (Asterisk node + DB/Web node); that's
  one profile, proven. Don't build four more nobody's requested.
  MariaDB version pinning could be added as a `dnf module enable mariadb:X.Y`
  step if a specific customer needs a non-default version — not before.
- **Dependency-graph solver** — the module count here (~4 scripts, ~10-22
  steps each) doesn't justify a generic graph engine. A hand-maintained
  sequential order with `check_step` gates is simpler to read, debug, and
  trust.
- **Benchmarking subsystem, HTML dashboards, support-bundle collector** —
  real product polish, but only worth building once there are paying
  customers who can tell you what they actually need from a report, rather
  than guessing at a comprehensive format upfront.

---

## How to use this document

Before adding a new architectural layer, ask:
1. Does a real customer need this today, or does it sound good in the
   abstract? ("Sounds good in the abstract" was the whole problem with the
   original vision doc.)
2. Can this be done as a small addition to what exists, or does it require
   rewriting tested logic? Prefer the former, always.
3. If deferring, write down the trigger condition — not "someday," but the
   specific thing that would make this the right call.
